d.why: On screen in two Agent Carter episodes, The Blitzkrieg Button and SNAFU.
Only in Agent Carter's The Lady in the Lake, where he is the case's culprit: the detective paid by Chadwick to dump Jane Scott's body as a copycat killing, who then takes Wilkes hostage and is shot.
On screen in three Agent Carter episodes: Monsters, The Edge of Mystery and A Little Song and Dance.
Only in Agent Carter's The Blitzkrieg Button (merely mentioned in The Iron Ceiling), as a condemned Nazi witness who tells Dooley about Finow before he is hanged; he leads none of the show's people.

Only in Agent Carter's The Iron Ceiling, as a Howling Commando on the Belarus raid taken hostage by Nikola, but kept because the wiki names him Captain Sawyer, commanding officer of Jim Morita's unit, and Morita has a file.
On screen in two Agent Carter episodes, Now is Not the End and Time and Tide.

Only in Agent Carter's The Iron Ceiling, as a Howling Commando on the Belarus raid who tells a yeti story and is killed by the girl assassin; he is a teammate, not family or a leader of anyone with a file.
On screen in two Agent Carter episodes, A View in the Dark and Better Angels (mentioned in Smoke & Mirrors).
Only in Agent Carter's The Lady in the Lake, as the medical examiner who examines Jane Scott's body and freezes to death; a helper in someone else's case with no family or boss tie.
Only in Agent Carter's The Iron Ceiling, as an SSR agent on the Belarus raid who meets Dugan and is shot by the girl assassin; a colleague, not family or anyone's boss.
On screen in two Agent Carter episodes, Now is Not the End and Bridge and Tunnel.
On screen in four Agent Carter season 1 episodes (Bridge and Tunnel, Time and Tide, The Blitzkrieg Button, A Sin to Err).

Only in Agent Carter's The Iron Ceiling, as a prisoner freed in the raid who explains Stark's designs, takes Sawyer hostage and is shot by Ivchenko; a side figure in the raid, and his only family is an unnamed wife.
On screen in two Agent Carter episodes, The Edge of Mystery and Hollywood Ending, and is also Joseph Manfredi's grandmother.

Only in Agent Carter's The Blitzkrieg Button, where he is the episode's villain: the smuggler who brings Stark home, extorts Jarvis, kills his own men and tries to murder Peggy and Stark until Dottie kills him.
Only in Agent Carter's The Iron Ceiling, as an SSR agent on Thompson's Belarus raid; a colleague with a few lines, and his only family is two unnamed sisters.
On screen alive in Agent Carter's A Sin to Err, where Dottie kills him, and again as his corpse in SNAFU when the SSR find her sniper nest in his office.
On screen in two Agent Carter episodes, Bridge and Tunnel and A Sin to Err (mentioned in SNAFU).
On screen in two Agent Carter episodes, A View in the Dark and Life of the Party (mentioned in The Atomic Job).
On screen in three Agent Carter episodes: Better Angels, The Atomic Job and A Little Song and Dance.
On screen in three Agent Carter season 2 episodes (The Lady in the Lake, A View in the Dark, The Atomic Job), and is Sousa's fiancee.
On screen in five Agent Carter season 1 episodes, from Now is Not the End to A Sin to Err.
On screen in five Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 7 episodes (701, 702, 703, 705, 706).
On screen in three Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 1 episodes (Pilot, The Magical Place, Beginning of the End), and is Mike Peterson's son.
Only in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s FZZT, where he is the victim the episode is about: the first man killed by the Chitauri virus, whose floating body starts the case and passes the virus to Simmons.
On screen in three Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 4 Framework episodes (418, 419, 420), and is Fitz's father there.

On screen only in the Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. finale What We're Fighting For, waking and playing with her parents, but kept because she is the daughter of Leo Fitz and Jemma Simmons, who both have files.
Only in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Parting Shot (indirectly mentioned in Hot Potato Soup), where he is the episode's villain, plotting to kill Russia's Prime Minister until Bobbi shoots him.
Only in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s The Singularity, as Radcliffe's assistant who books Fitz and Simmons in, sets off an EMP and is knocked down by Daisy; a helper who is nobody's family or boss.
On screen in two Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 3 episodes, The Inside Man and Parting Shot.
